title: Go: Defer, Panic, Recover
description: Use defer for cleanup, understand deferred call stack order, and handle panics with recover.

steps.title: Basic Defer — Stack Order
steps.description: Use three `defer` statements printing `"first"`, `"second"`, `"third"` in that order. Observe they print in reverse (LIFO).
hints: The output should be "third second first".

verification.failureMessage: Defer three prints and observe them print in reverse order.

steps.title: Defer with Function Call
steps.description: Define a function `printDone()` that prints `"Done!"`. Use `defer printDone()` in `main` and also print `"Working..."` before main exits.
hints: `defer printDone()` defers execution to just before main returns.
Deferred functions run even after a panic.

verification.failureMessage: Print 'Working...' and defer a function that prints 'Done!'.

steps.title: Defer for Cleanup
steps.description: Simulate opening a file: print `"opening file"`, defer `fmt.Println("closing file")`, then print `"working with file"`.
hints: Defer the cleanup right after the open operation.
This ensures cleanup runs even if the middle part panics.

verification.test: output.includes('opening file') && output.includes('working with file') && output.includes('closing file')
verification.failureMessage: Simulate open, work, close using defer for the close.

steps.title: Panic
steps.description: Write a program that prints `"About to panic"`, then calls `panic("something bad happened")`, and observe the panic message (output will show the panic).
hints: `panic()` takes a string or any value.
It stops normal execution and prints the panic message.
The output will include the panic message and stack trace.

verification.test: output.includes('About to panic') && output.includes('something bad happened')
verification.failureMessage: Print 'About to panic' and then call panic with a message.

steps.title: Recover
steps.description: Write a function `mayPanic()` that panics. In `main`, defer an anonymous function that calls `recover()` and prints the recovered value. Call `mayPanic()` and print `"After mayPanic"`.
hints: `defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { fmt.Println("Recovered:", r) } }()`
`recover()` stops the panic and returns the value.
"After mayPanic" should print because the panic was recovered.

verification.failureMessage: Recover from a panic and print both the recovered value and 'After mayPanic'.
